title: wg: pq-ciphersuites-06 L118 TBD5 and TBD8 (P-384, AES-256, SHA-384) carry the MLS_192 prefix, but...
description:
draft-ietf-mls-pq-ciphersuites (pq-ciphersuites-06), 3. IANA Considerations / MLS Cipher Suites. Editors' copy mlswg/mls-pq-ciphersuites at fb18956, L118.

Text: "| TBD5  | MLS_192_MLKEM1024P384_AES256GCM_SHA384_P384     |  Y  | RFCXXXX |"

Problem: TBD5 and TBD8 (P-384, AES-256, SHA-384) carry the MLS_192 prefix, but RFC 9420 registers the same classical primitives as MLS_256_DHKEMP384_AES256GCM_SHA384_P384 (0x0007). The draft does not explain the difference in convention, so policies keyed on the name prefix treat equivalent suites differently.

Suggested fix: Add a sentence saying what the security-level prefix means in this document (e.g. the level of the KEM) and that it differs from the RFC 9420 labelling of 0x0007.

Severity: low. Verifier: narrow (PR #14 ('we had consensus for SHA384 at 256-bit security level') shows that SHA-384 for TBD11 is a WG decision, and RFC 9420 0x0007 also uses MLS_256 with SHA384. The SHA-512 suggestion is dropped. What remains is that P-384 suites carry MLS_192 here but MLS_256 in RFC 9420.)

From MLS audit workflow wf_581e61f8-b25 (2026-10-21). Not yet reviewed by Mark; nothing posted upstream.
